description: The SAME production patch as mvc824-fileattachment-fk-guard-http, checked instead against test/WalkingTec.Mvvm.Admin.Test/FrameworkControllerUpdateModelPropertyPersistTests.cs, which calls _FrameworkController.UpdateModelProperty directly against a real BaseCRUDVM (FrameworkUserVM) and a real seeded FrameworkUser + FileAttachment pair. Included specifically to prove the runner's KILLED path is exercised against real production code in this same PR (mirrors mvc004-blocklist-empty-direct-crud-kill's rationale). PR #978 (#824 Part 2) review: the ORIGINAL red_test (UpdateModelProperty_FileAttachmentForeignKey_RejectedButNonAttachmentFieldStillSucceeds) can no longer detect this mutation alone -- Part 2's independent FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard boundary now also rejects the same forged write with an equivalent-looking message. red_test now points at UpdateModelProperty_FileAttachmentForeignKey_Part1GateAlone_RejectedWithBoundaryGuardDisabled, which disables Part 2 via FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard.Enabled = false for its duration, isolating Part 1's own contribution again -- the same mutation the HTTP-layer test structurally cannot see IS caught here because this test reaches the actual guarded code path directly. green_tests is the pre-existing UpdateModelProperty_ValidField_ActuallyPersists sibling test, proving this mutation does not collaterally break an ordinary (non-attachment) field edit.

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Admin.Test.FrameworkCont: #824 Part 1 alone \(boundary guard disabled\): PhotoId is a FileAttachment FK and must still be rejected

Actual type:<Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.OkObjectResult>.'. Confirmed identical on a second independent run_mutant.py invocation (determinism check).
